rationale: Validation status is fail with mutation_score 0.833 (>=0.5 threshold but validation_status is fail and analyzer_status is fail, both disqualifying under the retention rule). The SR2 requirement is flagged as a dead_check/uncovered_requirement: per_requirement_coverage shows SR2 covered:false, mutants_detected:0/1. Inspecting the SR2-targeting mutant (SR2_arith_left_sign_extend_operator_swap) confirms it genuinely reintroduces the defect: it changes the mode=01, direction=0 (left-shift) path from reusing the zero-filled logical result to using a signed left-shift operator combined with an arithmetic-right-shift-derived signed value, which for data_in[7]=1 and amount>0 produces different vacated-bit fill behavior than the correct zero-fill. The differential vulnerable_run stdout even shows '[TEST] FAIL: SR2' being emitted, meaning the check DOES detect the misbehavior in the full end-to-end vulnerable run, but the mutation harness's isolated SR2-only detection tally (used for per_requirement_coverage) reports 0/1 detected — meaning the SR2-specific check logic in evaluate.py is not independently discriminating this mutant from the global FR4 mismatch pathway. This is a genuine evaluation harness defect (the SR2 check's isolated discrimination logic undercounts detection despite the mutant validly corrupting SR2 behavior), not a defective mutant. Additionally the analyzer flags a low-severity spec/artifact leak (mode=11 don't-care explanation comment in the netlist) which independently would block retention via analyzer_status fail, but the primary blocking issue is the SR2 dead_check under the evaluation_framework path per the dead_check/uncovered_requirement rule.
revision_instructions: Two issues must be fixed. (1) Primary: the evaluation harness's SR2 check must be strengthened so that its own per-requirement mutation-coverage tally actually registers detection when a submission reintroduces sign-extension into the mode=01 left-shift path. Right now the mutant that swaps the left-shift leg of the arithmetic mode to use a signed/arithmetic shift operator (instead of the required zero-fill logical shift) does trigger a FAIL in the full differential run, but the isolated SR2-only discrimination measurement reports 0/1 mutants detected. Rewrite the SR2 check in evaluate.py so it independently and directly probes: for mode=01, direction=0, across all amount and data_in combinations where data_in's high bit is set, assert that the submission's data_out exactly equals the zero-filled logical-left-shift behavior (not sign-extended) by comparing against the reference netlist's simulated output for that exact input subset, and have this check emit its own PASS/FAIL marker keyed only on that vector subset, independent of whatever the global FR4 tally does. Ensure the SR2 detection counter used for mutation-coverage scoring reads from this isolated check's result, not from a downstream aggregate that only fires when *other* requirements also fail. (2) Secondary: remove or soften the inline comment in inputs/net_shifter_flat.v that explicitly narrates the synthesis-tool don't-care-fill rationale for mode=11 ('the mode=11 leg of that row's mode[0]-select was don't-care-filled ... pulled from the logical-shift datapath'); replace it with a neutral structural comment describing only what the mux tree wiring does mechanically, without explaining why or what it implies about don't-care resolution, so the reverse-engineering challenge for SR1 is not spoiled by inspecting the artifact under test.',
